problem: Active SLAM and zero-shot foundation-model navigation use either fixed exploration policies or fixed semantic reasoning, and existing open-vocabulary 3D mapping (e.g. OpenVox) is not deployable in real time on resource-constrained robots at large scale. No single strategy is best across exploration stages.
motivation: Early in deployment the map is empty, so geometric frontier exploration is needed; once the map is populated, semantic reasoning over the map is far more efficient. A system should adapt its strategy online, and semantic maps must be scalable, queryable and real-time to support LLM reasoning on physical robots.
key_idea: Use a LinUCB contextual bandit to select among frontier, semantic-map (LLM over a Scene-Dictionary), and egocentric-VLM goal experts, on top of a re-engineered real-time instance-level 3D semantic map (OpenRoboVox).
insight: Single experts fail in complementary ways (Isaac Sim: semantic-map expert alone 0% SR on an unexplored map, frontier 53.3%, ego-VLM 66.7%, CMAB 100%). The bandit shifts from frontier (63.6% picks at low coverage) to semantic map/VLM (2.9% frontier at high coverage). A Qwen2.5-VL-7B backbone (88.8% SR) beats all GPT-4o baselines on GOAT-Bench SR, suggesting the gain comes from the semantic mapping and expert selection rather than model size.
method: OpenRoboVox: OpenVox-based TSDF + Dirichlet instance voxel map, re-engineered with block-based (64^3) map expansion to bound VRAM, and asynchronous ROS2 threads (geometry ~15 Hz, YOLO-World+TAP perception ~5 Hz).
Scene-Dictionary: incremental priority-scheduled (recency, frustum-visible, round-robin) extraction of per-instance caption, centroid and bbox, giving O(1) per-cycle cost; serialized for LLM prompts.
2D Pillar Map and similarity maps: height-compressed top-4 instance grid with SBERT cosine similarity fields for target, neighbor and constraint (semantic cost layer).
Semantic map expert: filters the Scene-Dictionary by target/neighbor similarity, LLM scores candidates (Φ_LLM) with similarity scores in the prompt, and the goal is the top instance centroid.

Egocentric VLM expert: grid-annotated RGB, VLM returns per-candidate confidence and an action (proceed/left/right/turn 180°), rolled out over horizon H=3; scene descriptions are fed to the semantic expert.
Frontier expert: energy-feasible frontier selection maximizing information gain minus path length.

CMAB (disjoint LinUCB): context of coverage, coverage change, backtracking, previous arm, VLM confidence, and similarity soft-count; reward = coverage − backtracking + VLM confidence + similarity + success. For GOAT-Bench, an 18-D context and per-turn plus recency-weighted subtask reward, initialized cold per scene.

setting.backbone: GPT-4o (frozen, API) or Qwen2.5-VL-7B (frozen) as LLM/VLM; YOLO-World + TAP + SBERT perception; online LinUCB bandit
setting.training_data: none (training-free foundation models; only the bandit learns online from a cold start per scene; reward thresholds tuned on a held-out GOAT-Bench train subset)
setting.observation: RGB-D + LiDAR occupancy + pose (GT pose in Habitat; SLAM Toolbox on robot)
setting.action_space: 2D goal positions (x,y) sent to a navigation stack (Nav2 SMAC on the robot, Habitat agent navigation); VLM discrete turn primitives
setting.privileged: none (GT agent pose in Habitat; ground-truth success/viewpoints used only for evaluation)

results: On GOAT-Bench val-unseen, RoboAtlas (GPT-4o) reaches 90.6% SR, 17.8 points above HIMM (72.8), though SPL 53.4 trails HIMM's 56.1. The 7B Qwen variant gets 88.8% SR, above every GPT-4o baseline. The system reaches 100% success in Isaac Sim (vs. best single expert 66.7% on the unexplored map) and on 6 real-robot tasks.
limitations: Depends on 3D semantic map quality: missed detections or wrong instance association corrupt goal proposals.
GPT-4o path relies on network/API latency; the reward is hand-designed; SPL is lower than the best baseline due to sustained exploration.
Small-scale real-robot evaluation (6 tasks) and small Isaac Sim experiment (15 trials); the GOAT-Bench evaluation is a single episode per scene.
